root_motivation: Prod cannot say how many of its 4,771 tenants are people: every signup, funnel event, and claim-email row has no origin label, so three deploy-probe signups counted as real signups (coinciding to the minute with 0.93.0/0.94.0/0.95.0 releases), claim_email_events holds 0 rows, and oauth_funnel_events has no origin column at all. The fleet-IP signup-limit exemption proved fleet traffic was already known at the code level, just never written as data. Fix: a funnel_origin column (human|fleet|probe) written at insert time from the X-Mcphost-Origin header (only honoured from a fleet IP) and the existing fleet IP list, surfaced as a human-only headline plus a fleet/probe breakdown on admin.funnel and /healthz's funnel_7d, with a P1 backfill command for existing rows.
user_persona: Operator Joe, whose 10-07 digest reads "humans: signups 0 ... (fleet 41, probe 3)" instead of one conflated number; the deploy tool, whose smoke signup sends X-Mcphost-Origin: probe and is excluded from the human headline; a wm-build live verifier signing up from orch's IP, counted as fleet without sending any header.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the migration applied, When a tenant, funnel event, or claim-email row is inserted by any handler, Then it carries origin (funnel_origin) in {human, fleet, probe} and never unknown.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a signup from an IP in the fleet list with no header, When the tenant is created, Then origin = 'fleet'; and from an IP outside the list, origin = 'human'.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ftruth_ac02_fleet_ip_vs_human.rs -- two control::signup calls against a server configured with one fleet IP, one from that IP (no header) asserted fleet, one from an unrelated IP asserted human.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a signup with X-Mcphost-Origin: probe from a fleet IP, When created, Then origin = 'probe'; the same header from a non-fleet IP yields origin = 'human'.

additional.funnel_origin_is_a_new_column_not_a_repu: The PRD's own requirement 1 says 'migration adds origin ... to tenants, oauth_funnel_events, activation_funnel, claim_email_events' -- but tenants.origin already exists (migration 0012, synthetic/external) with dozens of existing callers/queries. Reusing that name for this PRD's human/fleet/probe verdict would silently corrupt every existing origin-keyed read. Resolved the same way migration 0032's signup_source resolved an identical naming collision with origin/origin_detail: a new column, funnel_origin, not a rename or reuse.
additional.activation_funnel_has_no_table_of_its_ow: The PRD's migration bullet names 'activation_funnel' as a fourth table alongside tenants/oauth_funnel_events/claim_email_events, but migration 0072 (PRD-mcphost-activation-funnel) added the activation stamps as COLUMNS on tenants, not a separate table -- there is no activation_funnel table to migrate. AC1's 'tenant ... row' already covers this; no fourth migration target exists.
additional.oauth_funnel_events_has_no_tenant_link_s: requirement 3's oauth_funnel_events table (migration 0053) deliberately carries no tenant_id (host-wide scalars, not split by tenant) and no source IP. The P1 backfill (AC5) therefore has no signal to reclassify an existing oauth_funnel_events row against and leaves the table read-only in Db::backfill_funnel_origin -- only its own insert-time classification (AC1, done going forward) applies.
additional.post_oauth_token_defaults_human_not_a_li: The shared POST /oauth/token success path (authorization_code and refresh_token grants, plus the JWT-bearer grant in assertion.rs) has never taken a ConnectInfo/HeaderMap extractor; widening every grant-type handler to thread an IP through for a funnel_origin no admin.funnel/healthz AC actually reads was judged disproportionate. It defaults to the literal string 'human' (never 'unknown', satisfying AC1) -- documented in record_oauth_funnel_event's own call site as a conservative simplification, not a live classification.
additional.host_progress_in_ac4_reads_as_admin_funn: AC4 names 'the digest and host_progress' as the two surfaces to update; no literal host_progress symbol exists anywhere in this crate. admin.tenants (a per-tenant listing that could also plausibly be called 'progress') is gated by PRD-mcphost-admin-schema-contract's own schema_version/additionalProperties:false contract and a pinned exact-field-list test (mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac01) belonging to a different, already-landed PRD -- adding a field there would require bumping that PRD's own schema version and rewriting its locked test, well outside this dispatch's assigned AC list. Read 'host_progress' as 'this host's own progress/funnel query layer' (the Engineering target's own phrasing, 'host_progress / digest query layer', as one thing, not two) -- i.e. admin::funnel (the operator-facing, per-tenant-aggregated report) and admin::funnel_7d_external (the literal /healthz funnel_7d field the digest tool reads).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an origin label matter if the fleet traffic was already excluded from the real/synthetic split?
five_whys_trace.a: It wasn't reliably excluded: the grounding shows three deploy-probe signups in the last 24h counted toward the raw daily total, and the fleet-IP bypass path (loop/mcphost-fleet-signup-limit) skips signup_events entirely for true fleet IPs, so the only durable signal of 'who signed up' was never written as data for either case.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't the digest just reuse tenants.source_class (already loopback/fleet/external)?
five_whys_trace.a: source_class answers 'is this safe to treat as a real customer,' computed from loopback/known-display-name/synthorg-client-name/fleet-IP together -- it has no way to distinguish a deploy-probe signup (fleet IP + a deliberate marker) from an ordinary fleet-IP signup with no marker, which is exactly the AC3 distinction the digest needs (probe excluded from BOTH the human headline and silently folded into 'fleet' counts, vs. reported on its own line).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does oauth_funnel_events/claim_email_events need their own origin instead of joining to the signup-time value?
five_whys_trace.a: claim_email_events already has a tenant_id to join through (and does, via a subselect at insert time); oauth_funnel_events deliberately has no tenant_id (requirement 3's own 'host-wide scalars' design) and no IP of its own at most call sites, so a live classification at write time was the only option for requirement 1's 'any handler' guarantee.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't the fleet IP list enough on its own, without a header too?
five_whys_trace.a: The fleet IP list already drives the rate-limit exemption and the loopback/fleet/external split, but it cannot distinguish a deploy release's own smoke signup from the ordinary synthetic-fleet traffic from the same box (orch/hub) -- the digest's whole point (AC6's user story) is reporting the deploy probe on its own line, which needs the tool to say so explicitly.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this wired when the fleet-IP exemption itself shipped (loop/mcphost-fleet-signup-limit, 09-27)?
five_whys_trace.a: That PRD's own scope was keeping the rate limiter from throttling the fleet's hundreds-per-hour signups -- a guard, not a reporting feature; the grounding's own why-chain (requirement 3) names this directly: 'the fleet exemption was built as a guard, not as data.'

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does funnel_origin reuse the existing tenants.origin column (the PRD's migration bullet literally says 'adds origin ... to tenants'), or get its own column?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Its own column, funnel_origin -- tenants.origin already exists (migration 0012, synthetic/external) with many existing callers; see hard_constraints.funnel_origin_is_a_new_column_not_a_repurposed_origin.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the P1 backfill (AC5) need to actually parse the deploy tool's release journal (on a different host, in a different repo) to classify historical probes?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- MCPHOST_DEPLOY_RELEASE_TIMESTAMPS (comma-separated unix seconds) is the portable mechanism; absent (the common case), the probe-backfill pass is a no-op and matching rows stay 'unknown', which the PRD's own Goals section explicitly allows ('stay queryable as unknown where neither applies').

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does 'host_progress' in AC4 mean admin.tenants' per-tenant listing?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- see hard_constraints.host_progress_in_ac4_reads_as_admin_funnel_slash_healthz_funnel_7d_not_admin_tenants; admin.tenants is schema-version-gated by a different, already-landed PRD and out of this dispatch's assigned scope.
